newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa nearbys end weaker as volume shrinks.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa nearbys end weaker as volume shrinks.

text.p: Cocoa players, undecided which way prices should head to, disappeared from both sides of the London market on Tuesday, axing the turnover.
The market just managed to gather a slim 717 lots which included 200 lots of AAs in March, traders said.
"People are unsure of the market. Everything is pointing to a downtrend but in the long-term the market is undervalued," said one trader.
Lack of direction in London shifted the focus to New York which traders said could provide some vigour, especially to March which holds the key for substantial switch activity in the coming weeks.
"Hopefully the March switch will start working. That'll kick-start the market," said the trader.

The attraction of March stems from its relatively high uncovered open interest of 27,000 tonnes which is likely to be partially rolled out. But a trade house with large physical stocks may also stir up the contract.

March finished three stg lower at 873 stg a tonne at midsession, hovering above a contract low of 865 stg touched on Monday. Other positions finished narrowly mixed in light dealings including a handful of offers by origins.
The market ignored estimates by commodity brokers GNI which put the Ivorian crop in 1996/97 at 950,000 tonnes leading to a supply deficit of 180,000 tonnes.

One trader said the figures looked "sensible", but disagreed with GNI's price projections pointing at the possibility of the second-month contract shooting up to between 1,050 stg and 1,600 stg in the coming months.
The New York-based General Cocoa meanwhile estimated Ivorian arrivals at 580,000 tonnes by January 4 from 717,000 tonnes at the same time last year.

In other news, southeast Asian cocoa producers revealed plans on Tuesday to set up a regional cartel, coordinated by Malaysia, to insulate them from price volatility and to put them in a better bargaining position.
But Indonesia, the world's third biggest grower, was undecided on whether to join.

The chairman of the Indonesia Cocoa Association, Litha Brent, said the country's 1997 production was likely to expand 10 percent to around 319,000 to 330,000 tonnes. The country has plans to become the world's second largest grower.
Technically, March is still prone to a slide to the 17-month low of 847 stg before oversold indicators start to work.
